doc.title: Sonny Rollins — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Appelbaum's thanks and the idea that it is all a gift
summary: Appelbaum says he is glad for Rollins; Rollins says his music is mostly a gift and that he must set himself straight.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: There’s a great old song, and I think it’s appropriate for me to tell you: I’m Glad There Is You.
Well...[chuckling]. See, now, he’s gonna say, see that’s, the problem with that is that you are making this ego thing again. “Well, gee, Sonny, you’re...you’re a good guy, and I’m glad–”

Yeah, but I mean it’s a, it’s a, sharing in that way you are putting me under the test to say, “Well, gee, man, I’m gonna put it on Sonny now to say, ‘Hey, man, you’re really a good guy.’” Well, okay, but it’s...I could, I could take the test. I’ll take the test.

Because, I don’t think, “I’m a good guy.” No, no. I don’t think that way. Inside of me: that’s where I want to be a good guy. When I think that, then I’m cool. Other than that, if you say, “Oh, Sonny, you’re really a great guy, man. Sonny, you’re really a great musician.” If I don’t feel it completely then...you know, it doesn’t, I got to feel it here. I’ve got do it here. I’ve got to be true to Sonny, and that’s my uh 80 years on this planet have gotten me now, see.
That’s still...I’m grateful. That’s all I’ll say.
I’m not saying you’re a great person. I’m saying you’re a great musician– even though I think so–I’m not saying that. I’m just saying I’m grateful that you took the time to talk with us today...
And I’m grateful for being able to tell you that.
Okay, well, I, I, I, I hope I’ve said something which...you know, like my music you’d say, “I like–” Okay, good. I hope, I hope I have, my music says something to you,

and evidently it does, and I’m grateful for that. But, see, most of that is–90% remember?–a gift. So, I can’t feel, “Oh, I’m a great musician.” No. That was a gift, see. I was given that talent. I didn’t work hard for it. I was given that. So, it keeps me in my place, too.
Well, let’s just say that I’m especially glad for the gift.
Well, thank you. I’m glad for the gift of you asking me questions. I’m glad for the gift of my friend here. I’m glad for the gift of my–you see? It’s all, we’re all...

It’s all a gift. And we all have it, man, and that’s why when you said, “Do I want to–glad to be a musician? What does it feel–?” Anybody is, is uh, you know, the, the, whatever we’re here for. Who knows what the fuck it is? I don’t know, but I know that it’s about inside of me. I know can’t put it on the world, and say, “Oh, the world is fucked up?” No, no. I gotta make me straight. That’s all it’s about. I know that.
